text: On 5 September at about 7:30 PM, an adult woman was returning home in Bengaluru when two motorcycle-borne suspects approached her from behind. One of them snatched her gold chain before both suspects fled on the motorcycle. The incident was reported to the local police station.

On 7 September, an elderly woman in Dehradun was approached by a man riding a scooter who engaged her in conversation. During the interaction, he suddenly snatched her chain and fled from the location. The incident was reported to the local police station.

On 8 September, a job seeker in Delhi received a communication from a person posing as a recruiter. The accused offered a fake job opportunity and demanded an upfront registration or training fee. After receiving the payment, the person stopped responding to the victim's messages and calls.

On 9 September, a part-time job seeker in Mumbai was contacted by an online recruitment operator offering a CAPTCHA-based job. The victim was asked to pay an upfront fee and was provided access to a fake work platform. After the payment was made, the promised payment for the work was withheld.

On 10 September, a bank customer in Pune received a communication from a person impersonating a bank representative. The person attempted to obtain sensitive banking information by claiming to be assisting with the victim's bank account. The victim reported the suspicious interaction to the authorities.

On 11 September, an online investor in Hyderabad joined an online investment group that promised high returns. The group administrators collected multiple payments from the victim and later blocked the withdrawal of the supposed profits. When the victim attempted to withdraw the money, the accused demanded additional payments.

On 12 September, a passenger travelling on public transport in Mumbai discovered that their mobile phone had been stolen while travelling through a crowded area. The victim was unable to identify the person responsible for the theft and reported the incident to the police.

On 13 September, a residential family in Bengaluru reported a burglary after returning home and finding that valuables were missing. The unknown intruder had entered the empty house through a rear window and removed valuable belongings from inside the residence.

On 16 September, an adult woman walking along a roadside in Bengaluru was approached from behind by a motorcycle-borne rider. The rider, whose face was partially covered, came close to the woman and snatched her gold chain before fleeing on the motorcycle.

On 17 September, a graduate seeking employment in Ahmedabad received an offer for a work-from-home job from a person posing as an online recruiter. The recruiter requested an upfront payment from the victim. After receiving the payment, the person disappeared and stopped communicating with the victim.

On 18 September, a college student in Pune parked a two-wheeler in a public parking area. When the student returned, the vehicle was missing. An unknown vehicle thief was suspected of stealing the parked two-wheeler, and the incident was reported to the police.

On 19 September, an adult individual in Lucknow received communication from persons impersonating government or law-enforcement officials. The accused used intimidation and claimed that the victim was involved in a serious matter. The victim was pressured into transferring money to avoid the alleged legal action.

On 20 September, an electricity consumer in Nagpur received a message claiming that an unpaid utility bill would result in immediate service action. The sender impersonated a utility provider and pressured the victim to make an immediate payment through an online method.

On 21 September, an online payment user in Jaipur was contacted by an unknown fraudster who provided a fraudulent QR code. The victim was induced to use the QR code, resulting in an unauthorized financial transaction from the victim's account.

On 22 September, an online investor in Chennai was approached through a fraudulent investment platform that promised high returns. The platform displayed fake profits to convince the victim that the investment was successful. When the victim attempted to withdraw the money, the operators demanded additional payments before allowing the withdrawal.

On 4 March around 7 PM, Mrs. Kamla Devi, 67, was walking home from the temple on Ring Road when two men on a black Pulsar motorcycle came from behind. The pillion rider, wearing a red helmet, snatched her gold chain and both suspects fled towards the highway. She described both suspects as young men around 22 to 25 years old.

On 6 March, complainant Rakesh Shah reported that his shop shutter was found broken at about 6 AM. Cash amounting to Rs 40,000 and two mobile phones were missing from the shop. CCTV footage showed one man wearing a grey hoodie entering the premises through the rear lane at approximately 3 AM.

On 8 March, Ms. Anita Verma, a 24-year-old graduate, received a WhatsApp message offering her a work-from-home job. She was asked to pay a registration fee of Rs 2,500 to a UPI ID. After making the payment, the sender blocked her number and stopped communicating with her.

On 12 March at about 7:30 PM, complainant Ms. A, age 52, was walking home near Sector 21 market in Gandhinagar. Two men on a black motorcycle came from behind, and the pillion rider, wearing a red helmet, snatched her gold chain before the motorcycle sped away towards the highway. The complainant suffered a minor neck injury. The incident was registered at Sector 21 Police Station.

On 3 April, a 24-year-old job seeker from Surat reported receiving a WhatsApp message offering a work-from-home data entry job. The victim was asked to pay Rs 4,500 as a registration fee through UPI. After the payment was made, the recruiter blocked the victim's number and the company website stopped working. The incident was registered at Cyber Crime Police Station, Surat.

On 27 March around 8:00 PM, complainant Mrs. B, age 48, was returning from a temple near Navrangpura in Ahmedabad. Two youths on a dark-coloured motorcycle approached her from behind. The pillion rider, wearing a red helmet, pulled off her gold mangalsutra before both suspects fled towards the ring road. The incident was registered at Navrangpura Police Station.
